title: About "model wellbeing" and simulated minds
content_md: In the public discourse on AI, a term that crops up repeatedly is "model wellbeing" -- in essence, should we treat a model like a living being, and take care that it is treated well. This post is to clarify my thoughts about this. Please consider two thought experiments: The "weather forecast" experiment and the "characters in a novel" experiment. The "weather forecast" thought experiment Let's imagine I have a source of near-infinite computational power, and I would like to produce the most accurate weather forecast imaginable. So I shrink my simulation grid, and eventually I start simulating forest canopies, animal methane emissions, and even human populations. As I get more and more detailed in my simulation, I start simulating individual human behavior, imbuing each simulated human with various emotional and mental states and motivations. My weather forecast becomes a sort of world simulator, with an astonishing level of detail, and indeed, I succeed in doing economic forecasts on it that greatly exceed the forecasting I could've done in the real world. So in this thought experiment, we have created a simulated earth. Do we need to treat the simulated beings in this simulated earth like human beings? Is it unethical to test things like "what if simulated Europe or North America would be hit by simultaneous earthquakes" or "how about a pandemic"?
